noah: heads-up: I'm seeing a flaky hang in the Go SDK generator streaming iterator when cancelling contexts during token handshake. tiny repro attached.

noah: gist of repro: call client.Generator().Stream(ctx...) then cancel ctx shortly after first token. sometimes Next() blocks forever and Err() stays nil. observed on local and CI.

rita: can you paste minimal snippet and any logs?

noah: snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, prompt)
go func() {
  for iter.Next() {
    if iter.Value() == "\n" { cancel() }
  }
  log.Println("done")
}()
// process exits hang
```

ben: suspicious. we used to rely on connection close to unblock the read loop. if auth refresh is in-flight the read may block waiting for server frames.

rita: UX options: add Close()/Abort() on iterator, or ensure Next() selects on ctx.Done(). both seem valid. Close() is explicit and works even if user passes context.Background().

noah: prototype wrapper I made that exposes Close() by cancelling an internal context works around it. will paste as part of issue.

ben: implementation: add Close() that closes underlying net.Conn/readPump and set Err() to context.Canceled. need tests for concurrent Close+Next+Err.

ci-bot: build #2301: repro job passed; attaching logs.

rita: I'll draft a PR adding Close() + docs note for quickstart recommending derived contexts or Close() on shutdown. we'll include test cases for handshake mid-auth cancellation.

noah: thanks—filing issue with repro and pprof.
